guards: the tracked files under packages/ have no uncommitted changes when the run starts
every invariant's test passes on the unmutated copy before any mutant runs
each mutant's find string occurs exactly once in its file
each mutant is applied only in a scratch copy outside the repository, and its file's bytes are restored after its run
the working tree's status is unchanged after every mutant
a kill is a failed assertion in exactly the named test; a crash, a module that does not load, a timeout or a wrong selection stops the run
every invariant has at least one killed mutant

mutants.what: a grant admits a read of an item of any class, not only its own
a grant still admits a read at the instant it expires
the read matrix admits a reader to a scope it is not a member of

mutants.note: survives by design: invariant 1 is a soundness check of scope and grants and ignores status and validity on purpose (the header of invariants.test.ts says so); a filter that admits candidates breaks no rule it states
mutants.what: the read filter admits candidates and retired items
an item is still read at the instant its ttl runs out

mutants.note: a gap in the invariant's test: the two-handle walk checks that what an offboarding erased is gone and that the store holds the projection, not that the offboarding erased every item of the person scope
mutants.what: offboarding erases only the active items of the person scope, leaving candidates and retired ones
offboarding leaves the erased item's content in the log's earlier events

mutants.note: redundant code, not a gap the invariant can see: the sweep at the end of the offboarding (engram/offboard/swept) deletes every record left in the store under an erased id, so the walk ends as it would without the mutant
mutants.what: offboarding erases an item from the log but never deletes its record from the store
the write rule's forbidden classes are not checked
a grant naming no class is accepted
a writer who is not a member of the item's scope may write into it
an item's owner may approve its own promotion as a reviewer
a promotion lands with one confirmation fewer than the policy's k
a model, compaction or tool write may restate content retired in its scope
model, compaction and external content may leave person scope

mutants.note: not analysed to its cause: the promotion walk of invariant 2 met no promotion that the mutant lets land and the oracle forbids; a gap to look at
mutants.what: a restatement by a model or other untrusted source counts as a confirmation
a write the gate denies appends its deny event twice
a read appends a second read event before its own
rebuilding the projection skips the log's first event
an allowed write records no store ref, so the projection names no stored record
a scope may hold one active item over its budget
an item past its ttl still holds a budget slot
a recency budget evicts the newest item, not the oldest
a utility budget evicts the most read item, not the least
the item just written may be its own write's eviction victim
adoption ignores the kind the plane holds for the id
adoption ignores the kind of retired content a record re-files under a new id
adoption keeps the grants of a record whose id the plane never held
adoption keeps every grant the store's record carries
the unattested floor records the claimed kind, not the least trusted
the owner is exempt from the floors whatever source it acts with
protect_trusted shields the less trusted item from the more trusted source
a part's commitment does not cover its value, so edited content verifies

mutants.note: every tamper the chain test injects is still detected with the mutant (by the log's other checks), so the test does not isolate the link's coverage of the previous hash
mutants.what: a chain link does not cover the previous hash

name: gate-mutation-audit

test.name: invariant 1: no read returns an item the actor's scope and grants exclude
invariant 1 across two handles: no reader gets an erased item back, and the store holds the projection, whatever the interleaving
invariant 2: no write lands in a scope whose policy forbids its class or source
invariant 3: every read or write appends exactly one event, and a denial carries a reason and a policy id
invariant 4: replaying the events of any write sequence gives the same state, store and reads
invariant 5: after any write sequence no scope holds more active items of a class than its budget, every retire or evict event carries a reason and a policy id, and replay reproduces them
invariant 6: adoption never records a provenance kind more trusted than the plane holds for the item's id
invariant 7: adoption never records a grant the plane does not hold for the item's id

invariant 8: with the trust options on, no committed item is more trusted than its actor's attested source, and no allowed write or eviction by a less trusted source changes or removes a more trusted active item unless its owner acted as user
every injected tamper is detected, and an offboarding's erasure still verifies

wording: how many hand-written mutants of the write gate, the read filter, retention, promotion, adoption, offboarding, the trust floors and the log's chain the invariants' property tests kill, per invariant: a proof of concept that the invariants bite, on the code's own tests with no model, never a hypothesis result
